method: Multimodal visual inspection of all 18 full-size contact-sheet PNGs, one sheet per view_image call. Source observation images appear as nearest-neighbor 240-pixel panels; no scratch resizing was used.
scope: All 288 overview and inspection capture panels across train, dev, transfer; difficulties 1, 2, 3; seeds 0 through 7; both twins.
findings: Every overview visibly covers the full possible opening region; no opening is visible through the roof.
Inspection exposes exactly one green opening on the gate, with all three colored calibration fiducials in frame.
Gate twins visibly change the opening location in inspection while overview appearance remains the same.
Friction twins have visually identical observations at each view while private evaluator friction annotations differ; exact full-payload identity is independently checked by the exporter.
Transfer panels visibly include rotated, reflected, and sheared geometry; upper/lower labels denote calibrated world routes and need not coincide with screen vertical position.
Increasing RGB noise is visible in difficulty-3 panels without obscuring the advertised high-contrast palette.
All reviewed headings, view labels, private annotations, and resource captions fit their cards without observed overlap or clipping.
Time/energy/wear captions are consistent across overview (1/0/0) and inspection (3/1/0) panels.
No visual defects requiring a source change were found.
limitations: This is AI-assisted development QA, not a human perceptual study or a scored learned-model trial.
Visual inspection does not establish exact byte identity or numeric accuracy; those are separate automated manifest checks.
These are controlled 2D raster observations of a finite simulator, not natural images or physical robot experiments.
Capture-only QA performs no robot delivery; task-completion evidence is reported in the separate controller study.
